subject: ibex mountain goat
title: What If We Brought an Extinct Animal Back? We Did. It Lived 10 Minutes

scenes.text: What if we brought an extinct animal back? We did, in 2003. It lived about ten minutes.
The bucardo was a wild mountain goat of the Pyrenees. By 1999 one was left: a female named Celia.
Scientists froze cells from her ear. In January 2000 a falling tree killed her. The species was gone.
Then they put her DNA into goat eggs. 57 embryos went into surrogate mothers. Seven pregnancies. Six miscarried.
On July 30th, 2003, one kid was born: a living copy of Celia. The first extinct animal ever brought back.
She couldn't breathe properly; one lung had grown a huge extra lobe. Minutes later the bucardo was extinct for the second time.

description:
What if we brought an extinct animal back? In 2003 scientists did. The bucardo, a wild goat of the Pyrenees, was down to one animal, Celia, when researchers froze cells from her ear in 1999; a falling tree killed her in January 2000. Her DNA was placed in goat eggs: 57 embryos, seven pregnancies, one birth by cesarean on 30 July 2003.
The clone had a lung defect and died within about ten minutes, making the bucardo the first animal to go extinct twice.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: Every clone would have been a female copy of Celia, so even a healthy one could never have restarted the species alone. Which extinct animal would you bring back, and what should we run through next?
